rationale:
Revision v2, responding to decomposition audit v1.

What the audit decided:
- It accepted the split and the assembly.
- It accepted ten of the eleven children together with their natural proofs.
- It accepted the statement and frozen Lean type of tangent_structure.
- Its only required change: tangent_structure's natural_proof must contain a complete proof of the C^1 approximation theorem (C1A). The proof must verify the hypotheses of the checked Whitney theorem and track the exceptional measure in the componentwise application.

What changed: nothing else. All eleven keys, lean_names, statements, lean_statements and dependency lists are unchanged from v1. The other ten natural proofs and their proof_key_steps are copied verbatim. Only tangent_structure's natural_proof and proof_key_steps are rewritten.

The new Part A of tangent_structure is the printed proof of Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, with every step made explicit:
- Rademacher: Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv.
- Borel remainder suprema Rsup_k, computed on a countable dense set.
- Egorov (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) and Lusin (SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, with closed regularity of L^n), applied to the partial derivatives on the bounded shells S_m.
- A closed, locally finite union A with L^n(R^n minus A) < eps. On A, Df is continuous and the Taylor remainders are uniformly small on compact subsets.
- These are exactly the three fields of SimonGMT HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f Df, so the checked Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney applies.
- The componentwise step uses tolerances eps_j with sum_j eps_j < eps, and {F != G} is contained in the union of the sets R^n minus A_j.

Part A is machine-checked. The scratch file /tmp/lipapprox-dec-v2/c1a/C1A.lean (392 lines, sha256 f68df457f4c51fd8bbe9ff6abb4174a9b6dd829c75ccf8630e7d49d68fa0bdc4) compiles with the pinned toolchain, Mathlib and SimonGMT, with 0 errors and no sorry. It proves:

c1_approx is also instantiated at Rn n -> Amb n l with eps = 1/(i+1). #print axioms reports [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for both. The supplied proof of Lemma 2.6 rests on facts it only cites: (F1) a.e. tangent planes, measurability and density, from Simon Ch. 3 Thm 1.9; (M) L^p monotonicity, from Ch. 4 section 4; (P) the pinched bounds 2.4; and the tools (Cov), (Ext), (Gr). On top of these it runs three analytic steps: the good-set estimate (6) (step 3), the flatness of the good set (steps 2 and 4), and the hole estimate (10') with its covering (steps 7-9).

How the children prove the selected statement (steps 1, 5, 6, 10 and 11 of the supplied proof):
A1. Fix n >= 1, l, p > n. Obtain:
 - delta_P from pinched_density;
 - (delta_7, C_7) from good_set_complement;
 - (C_8, delta_8) from good_set_flat applied to Submission.affine_approximation_lemma;
 - (eps_10, delta_10, C_10) from graph_hole_measure.
 Let D := min{delta_P, delta_7, delta_8, delta_10} > 0 and
 beta := min{1/4, 1/(32 C_8), min{1, eps_10}/(2 sqrt(l) C_8 + 1), D^(1/(2n+2))} > 0.
 Then beta^(2n+2) <= D, C_8 beta <= 1/32 and 2 sqrt(l) C_8 beta <= min{1, eps_10}. Put C := max{3 omega_n/beta^2, (1 + C_10) C_7/beta^2 + C_10}.
A2. Take L, K, U, V, H, delta, rho, q as in the statement. Then delta <= (beta L)^(2n+2) <= beta^(2n+2) <= D. Put sigma_0 := delta rho > 0, P := p_(T_0) with T_0 = rotatedPlane q, and tilt := integral_(B_(sigma_0)(0)) hsNormSq(p_x - P) dmu >= 0.
A3. Case A: tilt >= beta^2 L^2 sigma_0^n. Take f := 0; it is 0-Lipschitz and |f| = 0 <= K delta^(1/(2n+2)) sigma_0. By pinched_density (y = 0, s = sigma_0/2 <= rho/2) and graph_measure (f = 0), the left side is at most 2 omega_n (sigma_0/2)^n + 2^(n/2) omega_n (sigma_0/2)^n <= 3 omega_n sigma_0^n <= (3 omega_n/beta^2) L^-2 tilt <= C L^-2 tilt.
A4. Case B: tilt < beta^2 L^2 sigma_0^n. good_set_flat gives:
 (H) dist(x, T_0) <= C_8 beta L sigma_0 on spt V cap B_(2 sigma_0)(0);
 (G) |Q(y_2 - y_1)| <= C_8 beta L |y_2 - y_1| for y_1 in G and y_2 in spt V cap B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0).
 Here Q := I - P, G' := {y in spt V : integral_(B_(s/2)(y)) hsNormSq(p_x - P) <= beta^2 L^2 s^n for all s in (0, sigma_0/2]} and G := G' cap B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0).
A5. Let a(y) and b(y) be the first n and the last l coordinates of q^-1(y). By graph_coordinates (iii), and uniqueness from (i)-(ii), q^-1(y) = graphPoint a(y) b(y). So y = q(graphPoint a(y) b(y)), and by (iv) and (i), P y = q(graphPoint a(y) 0) and Q y = q(graphPoint 0 b(y)). By (i), (ii) and the isometry q:
 - |a(y) - a(z)| = |P(y - z)| <= |y - z|;
 - |b(y) - b(z)| = |Q(y - z)|, and |y - z|^2 = |a(y) - a(z)|^2 + |b(y) - b(z)|^2;
 - |b(y)| = |y - P y| = dist(y, T_0) (Mathlib Submodule.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist).
A6. For y_1, y_2 in G, (G) and C_8 beta L <= 1/2 give |b(y_2) - b(y_1)| <= 2 C_8 beta L |a(y_2) - a(y_1)|. So a is injective on G, and g(a(y)) := b(y) for y in G (g := 0 elsewhere) is (2 C_8 beta L)-Lipschitz on A := a(G). Moreover |g(a(y))| = dist(y, T_0) <= R_0 := min{K delta^(1/(2n+2)) sigma_0, C_8 beta L sigma_0}, by the height hypothesis of the lemma and (H).
A7. bounded_extension gives f with f = g on A, Lipschitz constant 2 sqrt(l) C_8 beta L <= min{1, eps_10} L, and |f| <= R_0 <= K delta^(1/(2n+2)) sigma_0. Also |f| <= C_8 beta L sigma_0 <= sigma_0/32. This proves the Lipschitz and sup conclusions.
A8. Let Fhat := q '' graphOver f univ. It contains G, since y = q(graphPoint a(y) f(a(y))).
A9. First term. Let F := q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 (sigma_0/2)). If y in B_(sigma_0/2)(0) cap spt V lies in G', then y lies in G and |a(y)| <= |y| <= sigma_0/2, so y lies in F. Hence B_(sigma_0/2)(0) cap (spt V minus F) is contained in B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) minus G'. By good_set_complement (T = T_0, b = beta^2 L^2), its mu-measure is <= (C_7/(beta^2 L^2)) tilt.
A10. Second term. graph_hole_measure applies (f is eps_10-Lipschitz, |f| <= sigma_0/32, delta <= delta_10) and bounds the second term by C_10 [mu(B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) minus Fhat) + tilt]. Since G' cap B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) = G is contained in Fhat, this is <= C_10 [(C_7/(beta^2 L^2)) tilt + tilt].
A11. Adding A9 and A10 bounds the left side by ((1 + C_10) C_7/beta^2 + C_10 L^2) L^-2 tilt <= C L^-2 tilt, because L <= 1. The constants beta and C depend only on n, l, p.

subproblems.title: Graph coordinates and the projection onto the rotated plane
subproblems.statement: For all n, l and every linear isometry q of R^(n+l): (i) graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') for a, a' in R^n, b, b' in R^l; (ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2; (iii) every z in R^(n+l) equals graphPoint a b for some a in R^n, b in R^l; (iv) the orthogonal projection P onto T_0 = rotatedPlane q = q(R^n x {0}) satisfies P(q(graphPoint a b)) = q(graphPoint a 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b')) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), ‖graphPoint a b‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 + ‖b‖ ^ 2) ∧ (∀ z : Amb n ℓ, ∃ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), z = graphPoint a b) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), (rotatedPlane q).starProjection (q (graphPoint a b)) = q (graphPoint a 0))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: elementary linear algebra for the contract's graphPoint / horizontalPlane / rotatedPlane (used by the parent proof whenever it writes q^-1 y = graphPoint(a(y), b(y)) and P y = q(graphPoint(a(y), 0))).

Notation. For a in R^n and b in R^l, graphPoint a b is the vector of R^(n+l) whose coordinate with index castAdd l i (i < n) is a_i and whose coordinate with index natAdd n j (j < l) is b_j (definition via Fin.append). Every index k in Fin (n+l) is of exactly one of these two forms (Fin.addCases). e_k is the k-th standard basis vector. H := horizontalPlane n l = span{e_(castAdd l i) : i < n}, T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(H) (Submodule.map), and P is the orthogonal projection onto T_0 (starProjection).

1. (i) Both sides are vectors of R^(n+l); compare coordinates. Subtraction in EuclideanSpace is coordinatewise. At an index castAdd l i both sides equal a_i - a'_i, and at an index natAdd n j both sides equal b_j - b'_j (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). Hence graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b').
2. (ii) For z in EuclideanSpace, |z|^2 = sum_k z_k^2. Split the sum over Fin (n+l) into the castAdd part and the natAdd part (Fin.sum_univ_add). For z = graphPoint a b this gives sum_i a_i^2 + sum_j b_j^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.
3. (iii) Given z, put a := (z_(castAdd l i))_(i<n) in R^n and b := (z_(natAdd n j))_(j<l) in R^l. By the coordinate description of step 1, graphPoint a b and z have the same coordinates at every index, so z = graphPoint a b.
4. (iv) First, graphPoint a 0 = sum_i a_i e_(castAdd l i) (compare coordinates), so graphPoint a 0 lies in H and u := q(graphPoint a 0) lies in T_0 = q(H).
5. All castAdd-coordinates of graphPoint 0 b vanish, so <graphPoint 0 b, e_(castAdd l i)> = 0 for every i, hence (by linearity in the second argument) <graphPoint 0 b, h> = 0 for every h in H.
6. A linear isometry preserves inner products (polarization identity), so for every v = q(h) in T_0 we get <q(graphPoint 0 b), v> = <graphPoint 0 b, h> = 0. Thus w := q(graphPoint 0 b) lies in the orthogonal complement of T_0.
7. By step 1, graphPoint a b - graphPoint 0 b = graphPoint (a - 0) (b - b) = graphPoint a 0, so graphPoint a b = graphPoint a 0 + graphPoint 0 b and, q being linear, q(graphPoint a b) = u + w.
8. T_0 is finite dimensional, hence closed, and its orthogonal projection satisfies P u = u for u in T_0 and P w = 0 for w orthogonal to T_0. Therefore P(q(graphPoint a b)) = u = q(graphPoint a 0). This proves (iv).
proof_key_steps: Coordinatewise description of graphPoint via Fin.append and Fin.addCases
(i) subtraction is coordinatewise
(ii) split the Euclidean norm sum over Fin (n+l) with Fin.sum_univ_add
(iii) read off a and b from the castAdd and natAdd coordinates
(iv) graphPoint a 0 lies in the horizontal plane and graphPoint 0 b is orthogonal to it
q preserves inner products, so q(graphPoint a 0) is in T_0 and q(graphPoint 0 b) is orthogonal to T_0
q(graphPoint a b) = q(graphPoint a 0) + q(graphPoint 0 b), and projecting onto T_0 keeps only the first summand

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of a contract rectifiable varifold: measurability, integrability, a.e. existence and density (fact F1)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l in N, U open in R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a contract RectifiableVarifold in U, mu = V.weight and p_x = V.tangentProj x. Then (a) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (b) for every linear subspace T and every compact K contained in U, x -> hsNormSq(p_x - p_T) is mu-integrable on K; (c) for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto some n-dimensional subspace, and mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) as r -> 0+ (V.HasDensity x (V.mult x)).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (C^1 Approximation Theorem) and its printed proof (Rademacher 1.4, Lusin, Egoroff, closed subset, Whitney extension theorem 1.6); Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 ("only if"), Remark 1.3, the proof of Theorem 1.6 ("=>"), Remarks 1.5(3), 1.8(1), 1.8(2) and Theorem 1.9; specialised to the contract's RectifiableVarifold and tangentProj. This is fact (F1) of the parent proof. Part A proves the C^1 approximation theorem (it is not cited). It constructs closed sets of almost full measure on which the derivative is continuous and the Taylor remainders are uniformly small on compacts. It then verifies the three hypotheses of the checked Whitney theorem and tracks the exceptional measure through the componentwise application.

Notation. M := V.carrier (contained in U), theta := V.mult (theta > 0 on M), H^n := muHE[n], mu := V.weight, so mu(A) = integral_(A cap M) theta dH^n for H^n-measurable A. On R^n, H^n equals Lebesgue measure L^n = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). B_r(x) is the closed ball, B^o_r(x) the open ball. eta_(x,r)(z) := r^-1 (z - x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). For an n-dimensional subspace T, p_T := T.starProjection. "T is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M, theta) at x" means HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x T: finrank T = n and, for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)), integral_(eta_(x,r)(M)) f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) -> theta(x) integral_T f dH^n as r -> 0+. By definition p_x := V.tangentProj x is p_P for the plane P chosen by Classical.choose when such a plane exists, and 0 otherwise. omega_n := unitBallVolume n = pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2 + 1). For a map f, Df(x) := fderiv R f x (Mathlib's Frechet derivative, 0 where f is not differentiable). For 0 < eps < 1 let f_eps, g_eps in C_c(R^(n+l), [0,1]) be radial and piecewise linear in |y|, with f_eps = 1 on B_1(0), f_eps = 0 off B_(1+eps)(0), g_eps = 1 on B_(1-eps)(0), g_eps = 0 off B^o_1(0); then g_eps <= indicator of B_1(0) <= f_eps.

Checked tools. These come from the pinned Mathlib and the pinned SimonGMT. All are sorry-free and use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
(Rad) Rademacher. A Lipschitz map between finite-dimensional real spaces is differentiable L^n-a.e. (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt). For any map f, the differentiability set is Borel, and x -> Df(x) and x -> Df(x)v are Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv, measurable_fderiv_apply_const). If f is Lambda-Lipschitz, then ||Df(x)|| <= Lambda (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
(Eg) Egorov (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto). Let S be a measurable set of finite measure and h_k strongly measurable real functions with h_k -> h at every point of S. For every tau > 0 there is a measurable t contained in S with measure <= tau such that h_k -> h uniformly on S minus t.
(Lu) Lusin (SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable). Let nu be a measure on R^d such that every measurable set S with nu(S) < infinity contains, for every tau > 0, a closed F with nu(S minus F) < tau. If A is measurable with nu(A) < infinity, h : R^d -> R is Borel and tau > 0, then there is a closed C contained in A with nu(A minus C) < tau and h restricted to C continuous. The hypothesis on nu holds in two cases. For nu = L^n, Lebesgue measure is weakly regular (Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt). For every finite Borel measure on R^(n+l), finite measures on metric spaces are weakly regular.
(Wh) Whitney (SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney). Let A be a closed subset of R^n, h : R^n -> R and D : R^n -> (R^n ->L[R] R) with HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h D, i.e.
 (W1) ContinuousOn h A;
 (W2) ContinuousOn D A;
 (W3) for every compact K contained in A and every tau > 0 there is delta > 0 with |h(y) - h(x) - D(x)(y - x)| <= tau |y - x| whenever x in K, y in A and |x - y| < delta.
 Then there is g : R^n -> R with ContDiff R 1 g, g = h on A, and HasFDerivAt g (D a) a for every a in A.
(S) Scaling. eta_(x,r) is a similarity with ratio 1/r, so H^n(eta_(x,r)(E)) = r^-n H^n(E) (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_homothety_image and isometry invariance). Equivalently, the image of H^n restricted to E under eta_(x,r) is r^n times H^n restricted to eta_(x,r)(E). Hence integral_(eta_(x,r)(E)) h dH^n = r^-n integral_E h((z - x)/r) dH^n(z) for H^n-measurable E and measurable h >= 0. For signed h, h is integrable on eta_(x,r)(E) iff z -> h((z - x)/r) is integrable on E, and then the same identity holds. In particular, let f in C_c vanish off B_R(0) and let r be so small that B_(rR)(x) is contained in U. Then, by (L), both sides of integral_(eta_(x,r)(M)) f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = r^-n integral f((z - x)/r) dmu(z) are finite and equal, since mu = theta H^n restricted to M (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ for the right side; theta is a.e.-measurable). Only such small r matter for the limits r -> 0+ below.
(L) Local finiteness. For compact K contained in U, mu(K) = integral_(M cap K) theta dH^n < infinity (V.integrableOn_mult). U is the union of the open sets U_m := {x : |x| < m, infEdist(x, complement of U) > 1/m} (m >= 1; infEdist to the empty set is +infinity). The closure of each U_m is compact and contained in U.
(UD) Upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 and its a.e. form Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside). Let lambda be a measure on R^(n+l) whose outer measure is Borel regular; this holds for every Mathlib measure on R^(n+l) (SimonGMT Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular). Let A be lambda-null-measurable with lambda(A) < infinity. Then limsup_(r -> 0) r^-n lambda(A cap B_r(x)) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x not in A.
 - Null-measurable sets are Caratheodory measurable for the outer measure: take a measurable T containing A with A = T lambda-a.e.; T is Caratheodory measurable, and lambda(t cap A) = lambda(t cap T), lambda(t minus A) = lambda(t minus T) for every t.
 - SimonGMT states the null set for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which is the outer measure of simonHausdorffMeasureReal n (Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure). Moreover simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = c_n H^n with 0 < c_n < infinity (Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, simonAreaNormalization_pos, simonAreaNormalization_ne_top). So its null sets are exactly the H^n-null sets.
 - Its density quotient lambda(A cap B_r(x))/(realUnitBallVolume n * ofReal(r)^(n:R)) is r^-n lambda(A cap B_r(x)) times a positive constant (ofReal(r)^(n:R) = r^n by ENNReal.rpow_natCast), so the two quantities vanish together.
(AF) Area formula (SimonGMT Chapter02).
 (i) For every map G : R^n -> R^N, H^n(G({v : G is differentiable at v and DG(v) is not injective})) = 0 (area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero).
 (ii) Let s be a Borel subset of R^n, and let G be differentiable at every point of s, with injective derivative there, and injective on s. Then integral_(G(s)) h dH^n = integral_s JG(v) h(G(v)) dv for every h >= 0, where JG(v) = areaJacobianAt G v = (det(DG(v)^T DG(v)))^(1/2) (weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative).
 (iii) A K-Lipschitz map on a set A multiplies H^n(A) by at most K^n (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). In particular, Lipschitz maps send L^n-null sets to H^n-null sets.

Part A. C^1 approximation (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5).
Claim A. Let n >= 1, N >= 0, F : R^n -> R^N Lipschitz and eps > 0. Then there is a C^1 map G : R^n -> R^N with L^n({x : F(x) != G(x)}) < eps.
Steps A1-A5 prove the scalar case. Let f : R^n -> R be Lambda-Lipschitz and eps > 0. We construct a closed set A with L^n(R^n minus A) < eps and a C^1 function g with g = f on A; moreover f and g are both differentiable at each a in A with derivative Df(a). The steps follow the printed proof (Rademacher, Lusin, Egoroff, closed subset, Whitney), with two refinements. First, L^n is infinite, so Lusin and Egoroff are applied on bounded pieces, which are then glued by local finiteness. Second, the remainder supremum is taken over all y (not only over y in the Lusin set) and computed on a countable dense set, which makes it Borel.
A1. Rademacher. Let B := {x : f is differentiable at x} and D := Df. Let e_1, ..., e_n be a basis of R^n and D_i(x) := D(x)e_i. By (Rad):
 - B is Borel and L^n(R^n minus B) = 0;
 - D and each D_i are Borel;
 - ||D(x)|| <= Lambda for all x;
 - f has Frechet derivative D(x) at every x in B.
A2. Remainder functions. For x != y put R(x,y) := |f(y) - f(x) - D(x)(y - x)| / |y - x|, and R(x,x) := 0. Then 0 <= R <= 2 Lambda, since |f(y) - f(x)| <= Lambda |y - x| and |D(x)(y - x)| <= Lambda |y - x|. Fix a countable dense set Q in R^n (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense). For k in N and q in Q, let phi_(k,q)(x) := R(x,q) if 0 < |q - x| < 1/(k+1), and phi_(k,q)(x) := 0 otherwise. Let Rsup_k(x) := sup_(q in Q) phi_(k,q)(x), which lies in [0, 2 Lambda].
 (i) Rsup_k is Borel. The set {x : 0 < |q - x| < 1/(k+1)} is Borel. The map x -> R(x,q) is Borel, because f is continuous, D is Borel and (L, v) -> L v is continuous. So each phi_(k,q) is Borel, and a countable supremum of Borel real functions is Borel (Mathlib Measurable.iSup). In particular Rsup_k is strongly measurable.
 (ii) Rsup_k(x) -> 0 for every x in B. Given tau > 0, differentiability at x gives r > 0 with |f(y) - f(x) - D(x)(y - x)| <= (tau/2) |y - x| for |y - x| < r. If 1/(k+1) < r, every phi_(k,q)(x) is either 0 or R(x,q) <= tau/2, so 0 <= Rsup_k(x) <= tau/2 < tau.
 (iii) If 0 < |y - x| < 1/(k+1), then R(x,y) <= Rsup_k(x). Suppose instead Rsup_k(x) < R(x,y). The functions z -> |z - x| and z -> R(x,z) are continuous at y (as y != x). So there is r > 0 such that every z with |z - y| < r satisfies 0 < |z - x| < 1/(k+1) and R(x,z) > Rsup_k(x). Since Q is dense, some q in Q has |q - y| < r, and then Rsup_k(x) >= phi_(k,q)(x) = R(x,q) > Rsup_k(x), a contradiction.
A3. Egoroff and Lusin on bounded pieces. For m in N let S_m := B cap {x : m <= |x| < m + 1}. The S_m are Borel and pairwise disjoint, L^n(S_m) <= L^n(B_(m+1)(0)) < infinity, and B is the union of the S_m. Choose eps_m > 0 with sum_m eps_m < eps (Mathlib ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable). Fix m.
 (a) Egoroff. Apply (Eg) on S_m to Rsup_k -> 0. The convergence holds at every point of S_m, which is contained in B, by A2(ii), and Rsup_k is strongly measurable by A2(i). This gives a Borel t_m contained in S_m with L^n(t_m) <= eps_m/2 such that Rsup_k -> 0 uniformly on S_m minus t_m.
 (b) Lusin. Apply (Lu) with nu = L^n on the Borel set S_m minus t_m, which has finite measure, to the Borel functions D_1, ..., D_n with tolerance eps_m/(2n) each. This gives closed sets C_(m,i) contained in S_m minus t_m with L^n((S_m minus t_m) minus C_(m,i)) < eps_m/(2n) and D_i continuous on C_(m,i).
 (c) Let K_m := C_(m,1) cap ... cap C_(m,n); as n >= 1, K_m is contained in C_(m,1). Then:
 - K_m is closed and contained in S_m minus t_m, hence in B cap {m <= |x| < m + 1}, so K_m is compact;
 - every D_i is continuous on K_m, so D is continuous on K_m: for v = sum_i v_i e_i we have D(x)v = sum_i v_i D_i(x), and a map into the finite-dimensional space of linear maps is continuous on a set iff all its evaluations are (Mathlib continuousOn_clm_apply);
 - Rsup_k -> 0 uniformly on K_m;
 - S_m minus K_m is contained in t_m union the union over i of ((S_m minus t_m) minus C_(m,i)), so L^n(S_m minus K_m) <= eps_m/2 + n eps_m/(2n) = eps_m.
A4. The closed set A := union over m of K_m.
 (a) A is closed. The family (K_m) is locally finite, because the open ball B^o_1(x) meets K_m only if m < |x| + 1. A locally finite union of closed sets is closed (Mathlib LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion).
 (b) L^n(R^n minus A) < eps. If x is not in A, then either x is not in B, or x lies in S_m minus K_m for m = floor(|x|). Hence L^n(R^n minus A) <= L^n(R^n minus B) + sum_m L^n(S_m minus K_m) <= 0 + sum_m eps_m < eps.
 (c) A is contained in B, so f has derivative D(a) at each a in A.
 (d) D is continuous on A. Let a lie in K_m, and let W := the union over j != m of K_j. W is closed, being a locally finite union of closed sets. Also a is not in W, since the K_j lie in the pairwise disjoint shells {j <= |x| < j + 1}. So the complement of W is a neighbourhood of a whose intersection with A is contained in K_m. Thus K_m is a neighbourhood of a relative to A, and continuity of D restricted to K_m at a gives continuity of D restricted to A at a (Mathlib ContinuousWithinAt.mono_of_mem_nhdsWithin).
 (e) Compact-uniform Taylor remainder. Let K be a compact subset of A and tau > 0. Then K is contained in B_(r_K)(0) for some r_K >= 0, so K is contained in K_0 union ... union K_(floor(r_K)). By A3(c) applied to these finitely many sets, there is k with Rsup_k(x) < tau for every x in K. Put delta := 1/(k+1) > 0, and let x in K and y in A with |x - y| < delta. If y = x, both sides of the inequality in (W3) vanish. Otherwise 0 < |y - x| < 1/(k+1), and A2(iii) gives |f(y) - f(x) - D(x)(y - x)| = R(x,y) |y - x| <= Rsup_k(x) |y - x| <= tau |y - x|.
A5. Whitney. By A4, A is closed, and the three hypotheses hold for h := f and D:
 - (W1): f is Lipschitz, hence continuous;
 - (W2): this is A4(d);
 - (W3): this is A4(e).
 That is, HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f D holds. (Wh) gives g in C^1(R^n) with g = f on A and Dg(a) = D(a) for a in A. Hence {f != g} is contained in R^n minus A, which has L^n-measure < eps. Moreover, by A4(c), {f != g} union {x : f does not have derivative Dg(x) at x} is also contained in R^n minus A; this is Simon's form of Theorem 1.5.
A6. Componentwise application and the exceptional measure. Let F : R^n -> R^N be Lambda-Lipschitz and eps > 0. If N = 0, take G := F, since R^0 is a point. Otherwise choose eps_1, ..., eps_N > 0 with sum_j eps_j < eps. Each coordinate F^j(x) := F(x)_j is Lambda-Lipschitz, since |F(x)_j - F(y)_j| <= |F(x) - F(y)| (Mathlib PiLp.norm_apply_le). A1-A5 with tolerance eps_j give closed A_j with L^n(R^n minus A_j) < eps_j and C^1 functions g^j with g^j = F^j on A_j. Put G(x) := (g^1(x), ..., g^N(x)). G is C^1 because all its coordinates are (Mathlib contDiff_euclidean). If F(x) != G(x), then F^j(x) != g^j(x) for some j, so x is not in A_j. Therefore {F != G} is contained in the union over j of (R^n minus A_j), and L^n({F != G}) <= sum_j L^n(R^n minus A_j) < sum_j eps_j < eps. This proves Claim A.

The Lean version also intersects with a Lusin set for the zero function, so that K_m stays inside S_m minus t_m even for n = 0. A final formalization can import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WhitneyExtension directly: it is sorry-free, but not prebuilt in the package, so Lake builds it on first use.

Part B. C^1 cover of M (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 "only if", and Remark 1.3).
B1. By V.countablyRectifiable, M is contained in M_0 union the union over j of F_j(R^n), with H^n(M_0) = 0 and F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) Lipschitz. For all j, i >= 1, Claim A (N = n + l, eps = 1/i) gives a C^1 map G_ij : R^n -> R^(n+l) with L^n({F_j != G_ij}) < 1/i.
 Then Z_j := the intersection over i of {F_j != G_ij} has L^n(Z_j) <= 1/i for every i, so L^n(Z_j) = 0. By (AF)(iii), H^n(F_j(Z_j)) = 0, since F_j is Lipschitz and H^n = L^n on R^n. Every v not in Z_j satisfies F_j(v) = G_ij(v) for some i, so F_j(R^n) is contained in F_j(Z_j) union the union over i of G_ij(R^n).
B2. Fix one of the C^1 maps G := G_ij and let O := {v : DG(v) is injective}.
 - O is open: if DG(u) is injective, then c_u := min_(|w|=1) |DG(u)w| > 0, every linear map L with ||L - DG(u)|| < c_u is injective, and DG is continuous.
 - G(R^n minus O) is H^n-null by (AF)(i), since G is differentiable everywhere and R^n minus O is its critical set.
 - For u in O choose sigma_u > 0 with B_(sigma_u)(u) contained in O and ||DG(v) - DG(u)|| <= c_u/2 for |v - u| <= sigma_u. The mean value inequality (Mathlib Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le) applied to v -> G(v) - DG(u)v on the convex ball gives |G(v) - G(v') - DG(u)(v - v')| <= (c_u/2) |v - v'|. Hence |G(v) - G(v')| >= (c_u/2) |v - v'| for v, v' in B^o_(sigma_u)(u).
 - By the Lindelof property of R^n, countably many such open balls cover O.
B3. Enumerate over all (j, i) and all chosen balls by k >= 1. This is a countable family; if it is finite, pad it with the empty ball B_k := B^o_0(0) and G_k := v -> graphPoint v 0, so that N_k is empty and all properties below hold vacuously. We obtain: M is contained in N_0 union the union over k >= 1 of N_k, where:
 - N_0 is a Borel set with H^n(N_0) = 0: a Borel H^n-null superset (Mathlib toMeasurable) of the null set M_0 union the F_j(Z_j) union the G_ij(R^n minus O_ij);
 - N_k = G_k(B_k), with B_k an open ball of R^n, G_k : R^n -> R^(n+l) of class C^1, and c_k > 0 such that |G_k(v) - G_k(v')| >= c_k |v - v'| for v, v' in B_k.
 Consequently:
 - G_k is injective on B_k, and DG_k(v) is injective for v in B_k;
 - G_k restricted to B_k is a homeomorphism onto N_k, since its inverse is (1/c_k)-Lipschitz;
 - N_k is sigma-compact (B_k is a countable union of closed balls), hence Borel;
 - DG_k is bounded on B_k (continuous on the compact closure), so G_k is Lipschitz on the convex set B_k, and H^n(N_k) <= (Lip of G_k on B_k)^n L^n(B_k) < infinity by (AF)(iii).
B4. Put M'_0 := M cap N_0 and M'_k := (M cap N_k) minus (N_0 union N_1 union ... union N_(k-1)) for k >= 1. These sets:
 - are pairwise disjoint;
 - are H^n-null-measurable (M is, by V.nullMeasurableSet_carrier, and the N_k are Borel);
 - cover M, with H^n(M'_0) = 0 and M'_k contained in N_k.
 This is the construction of SimonGMT Chapter03.simon_remark_1_3_nullMeasurable.

Part C. Blow-ups of N_k (k >= 1). For x = G_k(u) in N_k, let T_x N_k := DG_k(u)(R^n), an n-dimensional subspace.
C1. Claim: for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)), integral_(eta_(x,r)(N_k)) f dH^n -> integral_(T_x N_k) f dH^n as r -> 0+.
 Write f = f^+ - f^- with f^+, f^- in C_c nonnegative, and treat f >= 0; all integrals below are finite. By (S), and by (AF)(ii) for G_k on the Borel set B_k (where G_k is injective with injective derivative):
 integral_(eta_(x,r)(N_k)) f dH^n = r^-n integral_(N_k) f((z - x)/r) dH^n(z) = r^-n integral_(B_k) f((G_k(v) - x)/r) JG_k(v) dv.
 The substitution v = u + r w (L^n(r E) = r^n L^n(E)) turns this into integral_((B_k - u)/r) f((G_k(u + r w) - G_k(u))/r) JG_k(u + r w) dw.
 Let f = 0 outside B_(R_f)(0). The integrand vanishes for |w| > R_f/c_k, as |G_k(u + r w) - G_k(u)| >= c_k r |w|, and it is bounded by sup|f| times sup over B_k of JG_k.
 For fixed w: u + r w lies in B_k for small r (B_k is open), (G_k(u + r w) - G_k(u))/r -> DG_k(u)w, and JG_k(u + r w) -> JG_k(u) (JG_k(v) = normDet(DG_k(v)) is continuous, by continuity of DG_k and SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet).
 Dominated convergence along r -> 0+ (the filter is countably generated) gives the limit integral_(R^n) f(DG_k(u)w) JG_k(u) dw. This equals integral_(T_x N_k) f dH^n by (AF)(ii) for the injective linear map DG_k(u) on s = R^n, whose Jacobian is the constant JG_k(u).
C2. x -> p_(T_x N_k) is continuous on N_k. Indeed:
 - u -> DG_k(u) is continuous;
 - for an injective linear map L : R^n -> R^(n+l), P_L := L (L^T L)^-1 L^T is self-adjoint and idempotent with range L(R^n), so it is the orthogonal projection onto L(R^n). It depends continuously on L on the open set of injective maps: L^T L is invertible there, and inversion is continuous on invertible operators (Mathlib NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt);
 - u = (G_k restricted to B_k)^-1(x) depends continuously on x in N_k, by B3.

Part D. Unweighted approximate tangent planes (proof of Simon 1.6 "=>"). Let C be a compact subset of M with H^n(C) < infinity, and C_k := C cap M'_k for k >= 1.
D1. Let x in C_k, and let f in C_c with f = 0 outside B_R(0). Write eta := eta_(x,r). Since eta is injective, C is the disjoint union of C_k and C minus C_k, and N_k is the disjoint union of C_k and N_k minus C_k, we have
 integral_(eta(C)) f = integral_(eta(N_k)) f - integral_(eta(N_k minus C_k)) f + integral_(eta(C minus C_k)) f.
 All integrals are finite, since H^n(eta(C)) = r^-n H^n(C) and H^n(eta(N_k)) = r^-n H^n(N_k) are finite and f is bounded.
D2. By (S), |integral_(eta(C minus C_k)) f| <= sup|f| r^-n H^n((C minus C_k) cap B_(rR)(x)). This tends to 0 for H^n-a.e. x in C_k, by (UD) with lambda := H^n restricted to C (finite) and A := C minus C_k (lambda-null-measurable, and x is not in A).
D3. Likewise |integral_(eta(N_k minus C_k)) f| <= sup|f| r^-n H^n((N_k minus C_k) cap B_(rR)(x)) -> 0 for H^n-a.e. x in C_k, by (UD) with lambda := H^n restricted to N_k (finite by B3) and A := N_k minus C_k.
D4. The exceptional null sets of D2 and D3 depend only on C, C_k and N_k, not on f or R: vanishing upper density at x means r^-n lambda(A cap B_(rR)(x)) -> 0 for every R > 0.
D5. With C1, for H^n-a.e. x in C_k we get integral_(eta_(x,r)(C)) f dH^n -> integral_(T_x N_k) f dH^n for all f in C_c simultaneously. Testing with f_eps and g_eps (Notation) and letting eps -> 0 gives r^-n H^n(C cap B_r(x)) -> omega_n (Simon Remark 1.5(3)). Here H^n(T cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n for every n-plane T (see Part F). In particular r^-n H^n(C cap B_(rR)(x)) stays bounded as r -> 0. Since H^n(M'_0) = 0, these conclusions hold for H^n-a.e. x in C, with plane T_x N_k for x in C_k.

Part E. Weighted approximate tangent planes (Simon Remark 1.8(1) and Theorem 1.9).
E1. Borel representative. By V.aemeasurable_mult, fix a Borel function theta~ with theta~ = theta at H^n-a.e. point of M, and a Borel H^n-null set N_theta containing {x in M : theta(x) != theta~(x)}.
 For m >= 1 let E_m := (M minus N_theta) cap closure(U_m) cap {theta~ >= 1/m}. It is H^n-null-measurable, and H^n(E_m) <= m integral_(M cap closure(U_m)) theta dH^n < infinity by (L). Also M minus N_theta is the union of the E_m, since theta = theta~ > 0 there and M is contained in U. Choose a Borel E'_m contained in E_m with H^n(E_m minus E'_m) = 0.
E2. Lusin compacts. For each m and i >= 1, apply (Lu) with the finite measure nu := H^n restricted to E'_m, A := E'_m, the Borel function theta~ and tau = 1/i. The hypothesis of (Lu) holds because finite measures on metric spaces are weakly regular (Mathlib instance MeasureTheory.Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure; nu(R^(n+l)) = H^n(E'_m) < infinity). This gives a closed C_(m,i) contained in E'_m with H^n(E'_m minus C_(m,i)) < 1/i and theta~ continuous on C_(m,i).
 C_(m,i) is compact (a closed subset of the compact set closure(U_m)), is contained in M and has finite H^n-measure. Since theta = theta~ on C_(m,i), the restriction of theta to C_(m,i) is continuous.
 Hence H^n(M minus the union over m, i of C_(m,i)) = 0. Enumerate the C_(m,i) as C_1, C_2, ....
E3. Fix j. For H^n-a.e. x in C_j, the following hold:
 (alpha) Part D applies to C = C_j at x, with plane T_x := T_x N_k, where k is such that x lies in M'_k.
 (beta) limsup_(r -> 0) r^-n mu((M minus C_j) cap B_r(x)) = 0. To see this, apply (UD), for each m' >= 1, to lambda := mu (its outer measure is Borel regular) and A := (M minus C_j) cap U_(m'). This A is mu-null-measurable and mu(A) <= mu(closure U_(m')) < infinity by (L). Every x in C_j lies in some U_(m') (C_j is a compact subset of U), and A cap B_r(x) = (M minus C_j) cap B_r(x) for small r.
 These exceptional sets do not depend on f.
E4. Let x be as in E3. Let f in C_c with f = 0 outside B_R(0), and let r be so small that B_(rR)(x) is contained in U. By (S):
 integral_(eta_(x,r)(M)) f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = r^-n integral_(M minus C_j) f((z - x)/r) dmu(z) + r^-n integral_(C_j) f((z - x)/r) (theta(z) - theta(x)) dH^n(z) + theta(x) integral_(eta_(x,r)(C_j)) f dH^n.
 - The first term is at most sup|f| r^-n mu((M minus C_j) cap B_(rR)(x)), which tends to 0 by (beta).
 - The second term is at most sup|f| times sup{|theta(z) - theta(x)| : z in C_j cap B_(rR)(x)} times r^-n H^n(C_j cap B_(rR)(x)). This tends to 0, because theta restricted to C_j is continuous at x and the last factor is bounded (D5).
 - The third term tends to theta(x) integral_(T_x) f dH^n, by (alpha).
 Hence T_x, which has finrank n, is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M, theta) at x.
E5. Let Good be the set of x in M at which a weighted approximate tangent plane exists.
 - By E2-E4 and H^n(N_theta) = 0, H^n(M minus Good) = 0. Hence mu(complement of Good) = 0, as mu is absolutely continuous with respect to H^n restricted to M and mu(complement of M) = 0.
 - At x in Good, theta(x) > 0, so the plane is unique (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Therefore p_x = V.tangentProj x is the orthogonal projection onto it, which has finrank n. This is the first half of (c).
 - Moreover, for H^n-a.e. x in M'_k (k >= 1) the weighted plane is T_x N_k, by E3-E4, because the C_j cover M up to an H^n-null set.

Part F. Density (Simon Remark 1.8(2)). Let x in Good with plane T, and 0 < eps < 1.
 Since g_eps <= indicator of B_1(0) <= f_eps and theta > 0 on M, (S) gives
 r^-n integral g_eps((z - x)/r) dmu(z) <= r^-n mu(B_r(x)) <= r^-n integral f_eps((z - x)/r) dmu(z).
 The outer terms are the weighted blow-up integrals of g_eps and f_eps. They converge to theta(x) integral_T g_eps dH^n >= theta(x) omega_n (1 - eps)^n and to theta(x) integral_T f_eps dH^n <= theta(x) omega_n (1 + eps)^n, respectively. Here H^n(T cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n for every n-plane T and s >= 0. To see this, push H^n on T forward along the subtype isometry T -> R^(n+l) (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure); on the n-dimensional inner product space T, muHE[n] = volume (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); and volume(closedBall 0 s) = ofReal(s)^n ofReal(sqrt(pi)^n/Gamma(n/2 + 1)) (InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall), where sqrt(pi)^n = pi^(n/2).
 Letting eps -> 0 gives mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) as r -> 0+. These quantities are finite for small r by (L), so in [0, infinity] this is V.HasDensity x (V.mult x). This is the second half of (c).

Part G. Measurability (a). Define Pi(x) := p_(T_x N_k) if x lies in N_k minus (N_0 union ... union N_(k-1)) for some k >= 1, and Pi(x) := 0 otherwise.
 - The pieces P_k := N_k minus (N_0 union ... union N_(k-1)) are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, and psi_k(x) := p_(T_x N_k) is continuous on N_k, which contains P_k (C2). So Pi is Borel measurable. For a Borel set S of linear maps, Pi^-1(S) is the union over k of (P_k cap psi_k^-1(S)), together with the complement of the union of the P_k if 0 is in S. Each P_k cap psi_k^-1(S) is Borel, because psi_k restricted to the Borel set P_k is continuous, hence Borel (equivalently, P_k.piecewise psi_k 0 is measurable by Mathlib ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise). Pi takes values in the finite-dimensional normed space of linear maps of R^(n+l), so it is strongly measurable.
 - By E5, for mu-a.e. x there is k >= 1 with x in Good cap M'_k and p_x = p_(T_x N_k) = Pi(x). Here M'_k is contained in N_k minus (N_0 union ... union N_(k-1)), and mu(M'_0) = 0.
 Hence V.tangentProj = Pi mu-a.e., and V.tangentProj is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. This proves (a).

Part H. Integrability (b).
 - For every x, V.tangentProj x is 0 or an orthogonal projection, so its operator norm is at most 1; the same holds for p_T.
 - For a linear map A of R^(n+l), hsNormSq(A) = sum_(i < n+l) |A e_i|^2 <= (n + l) ||A||^2. So 0 <= hsNormSq(p_x - p_T) <= 4(n + l) for all x.
 - The map A -> hsNormSq(A - p_T) is continuous, so by (a) x -> hsNormSq(p_x - p_T) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable.
 - For compact K contained in U, mu(K) < infinity by (L).
 A bounded a.e.-strongly measurable function is integrable on a set of finite measure, which proves (b).
proof_key_steps: C^1 approximation, Part A: Rademacher; Borel remainder suprema Rsup_k computed on a countable dense set; Egorov and Lusin (partial derivatives) on the bounded shells S_m; closed locally finite union A with L^n(R^n minus A) < eps

Df is continuous on A (each K_m is a relative neighbourhood in A) and the Taylor remainders are uniform on compacts of A: these are the three fields of HasWhitneyC1Compatibility, so the checked Whitney theorem gives g in C^1 with g = f on A
Componentwise application with tolerances eps_j, sum_j eps_j < eps: L^n({F != G}) <= sum_j L^n(R^n minus A_j) < eps
C^1 cover: M lies in N_0 union countably many bi-Lipschitz C^1 images N_k = G_k(B_k) (Z_j null, critical images null, inverse-function estimate, Lindelof); disjoint null-measurable pieces M'_k
Blow-ups of N_k converge to T_x N_k (area formula, substitution, dominated convergence), and x -> p_(T_x N_k) is continuous on N_k
Upper density theorem: a compact C in M of finite H^n-measure has approximate tangent plane T_x N_k and density omega_n at H^n-a.e. x

Borel representative of theta, Lusin compacts on which theta is continuous, and the localized upper density theorem for mu: weighted approximate tangent planes exist H^n-a.e., hence mu-a.e., and are unique since theta > 0
Radial cut-offs squeezing the unit ball give mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x), i.e. HasDensity
tangentProj agrees mu-a.e. with the Borel map Pi, giving (a); a bounded integrand and finite mass on compacts give (b)

subproblems.title: Monotonicity inequalities for L^p mean curvature under the Allard hypotheses (fact M)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l, p > n, U open, V a contract rectifiable varifold in U with generalized mean curvature H, delta > 0 and rho such that 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho) holds, and Lambda with 4 p delta/(p - n) <= Lambda <= 1. Let y in R^(n+l), R > 0 with B_R(y) contained in B_rho(0), and 0 < s <= r < R. With mu = V.weight and closed balls: (I) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= e^(2 Lambda) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda; (II) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) <= e^(2 Lambda) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda + e^(2 Lambda) integral over B_r(y) minus B_s(y) of |(x - y) - p_x(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu(x); (III) if y in spt V then e^(-Lambda)(omega_n - Lambda) <= s^-n mu(B_s(y)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ Λ : ℝ), 0 < δ → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → 4 * p * δ / (p - n) ≤ Λ → Λ ≤ 1 → ∀ (y : Amb n ℓ) (R : ℝ), 0 < R → closedBall y R ⊆ closedBall 0 ρ → ∀ s r : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ r → r < R → V.weight.real (closedBall y s) / s ^ n ≤ Real.exp (2 * Λ) * (V.weight.real (closedBall y r) / r ^ n) + 2 * Real.exp Λ * Λ ∧ V.weight.real (closedBall y r) / r ^ n ≤ Real.exp (2 * Λ) * (V.weight.real (closedBall y s) / s ^ n) + 2 * Real.exp Λ * Λ + Real.exp (2 * Λ) * ∫ x in closedBall y r \ closedBall y s, ‖(x - y) - V.tangentProj x (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ (n + 2) ∂V.weight ∧ (y ∈ V.support → Real.exp (-Λ) * (unitBallVolume n - Λ) ≤ V.weight.real (closedBall y s) / s ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 3.1-3.6 (radial test field) and 4.1-4.10 (L^p mean curvature), with the coefficient in front of Lambda in 4.2 equal to kappa = (p-n)/(4p), the value required by the integration after 4.4 (as in SimonGMT Chapter04 lpMeanCurvatureKappa / LpAnnularCorrection). This is facts (M.i)-(M.v) of the parent proof, in the form used there. To avoid fixing one integrating factor in the limit eps -> 0, all estimates are derived for each cutoff and only the eps-independent bounds are passed to the limit.

Notation. mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; p_x^perp := I - p_x; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0; K(z,t) := (t^(p-n) integral_(B_t(z)) |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) (V.scaledLpNorm H p z t); B_t(z) closed balls. Hypotheses: n >= 1, p > n, U open, V has generalized mean curvature H in U, 2.3 holds (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, so rho > 0, B_rho(0) contained in U, theta >= 1 mu-a.e., 0 in spt V, K(0,rho) <= delta), delta > 0, 4p delta/(p-n) <= Lambda <= 1 (so Lambda > 0 and kappa Lambda >= delta), B_R(y) contained in B_rho(0), R > 0, 0 < s <= r < R.

0. Preliminaries.
 (0a) Since R > 0 and B_R(y) is contained in B_rho(0), |y| <= rho - R; in particular R <= rho and y lies in the open ball B^o_rho(0).
 (0b) If t > 0 and B_t(z) is contained in B_rho(0), then t <= rho and K(z,t)^p = t^(p-n) integral_(B_t(z)) |H|^p <= (t/rho)^(p-n) rho^(p-n) integral_(B_rho(0)) |H|^p <= (t/rho)^(p-n) delta^p, so K(z,t) <= (t/rho)^(1-n/p) delta <= kappa Lambda (t/rho)^(1-n/p). In particular integral_(B_rho(0)) |H|^p dmu < infinity.
 (0c) mu(B) < infinity for every closed ball B contained in B_rho(0) (compact subset of U), and H is mu-integrable on such balls (HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature includes local integrability of H on U).
 (0d) By the tangent-structure child (lip_approx_tangent_structure): x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace and mu(B_t(x))/(omega_n t^n) -> theta(x) as t -> 0+. For every x, p_x is 0 or an orthogonal projection, so |p_x^perp v| <= |v|.

1. Cutoffs and the functions I, J, e. Let z be a point and R_z > 0 with B_(R_z)(z) contained in B_rho(0), and let Lambda_z in (0,1] satisfy K(z,R_z) <= kappa Lambda_z. Fix eps in (0,1] and phi in C^1(R, [0,1]) with phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1], phi = 0 on [1+eps, infinity), phi' <= 0 (for instance phi(u) = psi((u-1)/eps) with psi(v) = 1 for v <= 0, 1 - 3v^2 + 2v^3 for 0 <= v <= 1, 0 for v >= 1); then integral (-phi') = 1. For t in (0, R_z/(1+eps)) put
 I(t) := integral phi(|x - z|/t) dmu(x), J(t) := integral phi(|x - z|/t) g(x) dmu(x), g(x) := |p_x^perp(x - z)|^2/|x - z|^2 (g(z) := 0), e(t) := t^(-n-1) integral phi(|x - z|/t) <x - z, H(x)> dmu(x).
 The integrands vanish outside B_((1+eps)t)(z), contained in B_(R_z)(z), are mu-measurable by (0d), and 0 <= g <= 1. With psi_t(x) := d/dt[phi(|x - z|/t)] = -(|x - z|/t^2) phi'(|x - z|/t) >= 0 and |psi_t| <= (1+eps) sup|phi'|/t, differentiation under the integral sign (dominated convergence, mu(B_(R_z)(z)) < infinity) shows that I and J are C^1 with I'(t) = integral psi_t dmu and J'(t) = integral psi_t g dmu >= 0, and e is continuous (dominated by |x - z||H| on B_(R_z)(z)).
2. Radial test field (Simon 3.2). X_t(x) := phi(|x - z|/t)(x - z). It is C^1 (phi(|x - z|/t) = 1 on the open ball B^o_t(z), and |x - z| is smooth away from z), has compact support and tsupport X_t is contained in B_((1+eps)t)(z), a subset of U. For x with r_x := |x - z| > 0, DX_t(x)v = phi(r_x/t) v + (phi'(r_x/t)/(t r_x)) <x - z, v> (x - z); near z, DX_t = identity. Hence at every x where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace (mu-a.e. by (0d)), using trace(p_x) = n, trace((v -> <a,v> b) o p_x) = <a, p_x b> and <v, p_x v> = |p_x v|^2 = |v|^2 - |p_x^perp v|^2:
 divM X_t(x) = trace(DX_t(x) o p_x) = n phi(r_x/t) + (r_x/t) phi'(r_x/t)(1 - g(x)) = n phi(r_x/t) - t psi_t(x) + t psi_t(x) g(x).
3. First variation (Simon 3.14, 4.1). X_t is admissible in the definition of generalized mean curvature, so integral divM X_t dmu = - integral <X_t, H> dmu. By step 2 this reads n I(t) - t I'(t) + t J'(t) = - t^(n+1) e(t), i.e.
 (3.1) (t^-n I(t))' = t^-n J'(t) + e(t) for t in (0, R_z/(1+eps)).
4. Hoelder estimate (Simon 4.2-4.3 with kappa). On the support of phi(|x - z|/t), |x - z| <= (1+eps)t <= 2t and phi^(p/(p-1)) <= phi. Hoelder gives |e(t)| <= 2 t^-n (integral_(B_(R_z)(z)) |H|^p)^(1/p) I(t)^(1-1/p) = 2 t^(-n/p) (integral_(B_(R_z)(z)) |H|^p)^(1/p) (t^-n I(t))^(1-1/p). As R_z^(1-n/p) (integral_(B_(R_z)(z)) |H|^p)^(1/p) = K(z,R_z) <= kappa Lambda_z and a^(1-1/p) <= 1 + a for a >= 0:
 (4.1) |e(t)| <= 2 kappa Lambda_z R_z^-1 (t/R_z)^(-n/p) (1 + t^-n I(t)).
5. Integrating factor (Simon 4.3-4.6). Put a(t) := -e(t)/(1 + t^-n I(t)), continuous with |a(t)| <= 2 kappa Lambda_z R_z^-1 (t/R_z)^(-n/p), which is integrable near 0 because n/p < 1. Let A(t) := integral_0^t a and F(t) := exp(A(t)). Since integral_0^t 2 kappa Lambda_z R_z^-1 (tau/R_z)^(-n/p) dtau = 2 kappa Lambda_z (p/(p-n)) (t/R_z)^(1-n/p) = (Lambda_z/2)(t/R_z)^(1-n/p), we get |A(t)| <= (Lambda_z/2)(t/R_z)^(1-n/p) <= Lambda_z/2, hence
 (5.1) e^(-Lambda_z/2) <= F(t) <= e^(Lambda_z/2) and |F(t) - 1| <= e^(|A|) |A| <= Lambda_z (t/R_z)^(1-n/p) <= Lambda_z (as e^(1/2)/2 < 1 and Lambda_z <= 1).
 Let Phi(t) := F(t) t^-n I(t) + F(t) - 1 = F(t)(t^-n I(t) + 1) - 1. By (3.1), Phi' = F a (t^-n I + 1) + F (t^-n J' + e) = F t^-n J' >= 0, because a (t^-n I + 1) = -e. Hence for 0 < s' <= r' < R_z/(1+eps):
 (5.2) Phi(r') - Phi(s') = integral_(s')^(r') F(t) t^-n J'(t) dt, which lies in [0, e^(Lambda_z/2) integral_(s')^(r') t^-n J'(t) dt].
6. The annular integral (Simon 3.5-3.6). By Tonelli, integral_(s')^(r') t^-n J'(t) dt = integral g(x) (integral_(s')^(r') t^-n psi_t(x) dt) dmu(x). For x != z with rho_x := |x - z|, the substitution u = rho_x/t gives integral_(s')^(r') t^-n psi_t(x) dt = rho_x^-n integral_(rho_x/r')^(rho_x/s') u^n (-phi'(u)) du. Since -phi' >= 0 vanishes off [1, 1+eps] and has integral 1, this is 0 if rho_x <= s' or rho_x >= (1+eps) r', and at most (1+eps)^n rho_x^-n otherwise. Therefore
 (6.1) integral_(s')^(r') t^-n J'(t) dt <= (1+eps)^n D_eps(s',r'), D_eps(s',r') := integral_(B_((1+eps)r')(z) minus B_(s')(z)) |p_x^perp(x - z)|^2 |x - z|^(-n-2) dmu(x).
7. Inequalities for fixed eps. From (5.1), (5.2), (6.1), for 0 < s' <= r' < R_z/(1+eps):
 (7.1) F(s') s'^-n I(s') <= F(r') r'^-n I(r') + (F(r') - 1) - (F(s') - 1) <= e^(Lambda_z/2) r'^-n I(r') + 2 Lambda_z, hence s'^-n I(s') <= e^(Lambda_z) r'^-n I(r') + 2 e^(Lambda_z/2) Lambda_z;
 (7.2) F(r') r'^-n I(r') <= F(s') s'^-n I(s') + 2 Lambda_z + e^(Lambda_z/2)(1+eps)^n D_eps(s',r'), hence r'^-n I(r') <= e^(Lambda_z) s'^-n I(s') + 2 e^(Lambda_z/2) Lambda_z + e^(Lambda_z)(1+eps)^n D_eps(s',r').
8. Limit eps -> 0 (general inequalities). Since the indicator of [0,1] <= phi <= indicator of [0,1+eps], mu(B_t(z)) <= I(t) <= mu(B_((1+eps)t)(z)), and mu(B_((1+eps)t)(z)) decreases to mu(B_t(z)) as eps -> 0 (closed balls decrease to the closed ball; finite measure). Similarly D_eps(s',r') decreases to D(s',r') := integral_(B_(r')(z) minus B_(s')(z)) |p_x^perp(x - z)|^2 |x - z|^(-n-2) dmu (integrand <= s'^-n there, finite measure). Given 0 < s' <= r' < R_z, every small eps satisfies (1+eps) r' < R_z, and the constants in (7.1)-(7.2) do not depend on eps. Using mu(B_(s'))<= I(s') and I(r') -> mu(B_(r')) in (7.1), and mu(B_(r')) <= I(r'), I(s') -> mu(B_(s')), (1+eps)^n D_eps -> D in (7.2), we obtain for 0 < s' <= r' < R_z:
 (G1) s'^-n mu(B_(s')(z)) <= e^(Lambda_z) r'^-n mu(B_(r')(z)) + 2 e^(Lambda_z/2) Lambda_z;
 (G2) r'^-n mu(B_(r')(z)) <= e^(Lambda_z) s'^-n mu(B_(s')(z)) + 2 e^(Lambda_z/2) Lambda_z + e^(Lambda_z) D(s',r').
9. First and second assertions. Apply step 8 with z = y, R_z = R, Lambda_z = Lambda; this is allowed because K(y,R) <= kappa Lambda by (0b). Since Lambda >= 0, e^Lambda <= e^(2 Lambda) and e^(Lambda/2) <= e^Lambda, so (G1) and (G2) with s' = s, r' = r give the first two assertions, with mu(B_t(y)) = V.weight.real(closedBall y t) (finite by (0c)) and D(s,r) the integral over closedBall y r minus closedBall y s.
10. Lower density at support points (Simon 4.9, 4.10(1)). Let w in spt V with |w| < rho. Claim: liminf_(tau -> 0) tau^-n mu(B_tau(w)) >= omega_n.
 (10a) By (0d) and theta >= 1 mu-a.e. (2.3), the set Good' of x with mu(B_t(x))/(omega_n t^n) -> theta(x) >= 1 has mu-null complement; at x in Good', t^-n mu(B_t(x)) -> omega_n theta(x) >= omega_n.
 (10b) Let tau > 0 with 3 tau < rho - |w|. For x with |x - w| <= tau, B_(2 tau)(x) is contained in B_rho(0); put Lambda_tau := Lambda (2 tau/rho)^(1-n/p) in (0,1]; by (0b), K(x, 2 tau) <= kappa Lambda_tau, so (G1) applies at z = x, R_z = 2 tau, Lambda_z = Lambda_tau: for 0 < t <= tau, t^-n mu(B_t(x)) <= e^(Lambda_tau) tau^-n mu(B_tau(x)) + 2 e^(Lambda_tau/2) Lambda_tau. If x in Good', letting t -> 0 gives omega_n <= e^(Lambda_tau) tau^-n mu(B_tau(x)) + 2 e^(Lambda_tau/2) Lambda_tau.
 (10c) Since w in spt V is contained in spt mu, every open ball around w has positive mu-measure, so by (10a) there are x_k in Good' with x_k -> w. For |x_k - w| <= tau, B_tau(x_k) is contained in B_(tau + |x_k - w|)(w), and mu(B_(tau + eta)(w)) decreases to mu(B_tau(w)) as eta -> 0. Applying (10b) to x_k and letting k -> infinity: omega_n <= e^(Lambda_tau) tau^-n mu(B_tau(w)) + 2 e^(Lambda_tau/2) Lambda_tau. As tau -> 0, Lambda_tau -> 0, which proves the claim.
11. Third assertion. Let y in V.support and 0 < s < R (s <= r < R). By (0a), |y| < rho, so step 10 applies at w = y. Fix eps with (1+eps)s < R and use the objects of steps 1-7 with z = y, R_z = R, Lambda_z = Lambda. For 0 < t <= s, (5.2) and (5.1) give Phi(s) >= Phi(t) = F(t) t^-n I(t) + F(t) - 1 >= (1 - Lambda (t/R)^(1-n/p)) t^-n mu(B_t(y)) - Lambda (t/R)^(1-n/p) (using I(t) >= mu(B_t(y))). Taking liminf as t -> 0 and using step 10: Phi(s) >= omega_n. Hence F(s) s^-n I(s) >= omega_n - (F(s) - 1) >= omega_n - Lambda. If omega_n - Lambda <= 0 the third assertion holds trivially (its left side is <= 0 <= its right side). Otherwise s^-n I(s) >= (omega_n - Lambda)/F(s) >= e^(-Lambda/2)(omega_n - Lambda) >= e^(-Lambda)(omega_n - Lambda), and as I(s) <= mu(B_((1+eps)s)(y)) -> mu(B_s(y)) when eps -> 0, we get s^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= e^(-Lambda)(omega_n - Lambda).
proof_key_steps: Lp smallness propagates to sub-balls: K(z,t) <= (t/rho)^(1-n/p) delta <= kappa Lambda (t/rho)^(1-n/p)
Radial C^1 test field X_t = phi(|x-z|/t)(x-z); divM X_t = n phi - t psi_t + t psi_t g mu-a.e. (tangent-structure child)
First variation gives (t^-n I)' = t^-n J' + e
Hoelder with kappa = (p-n)/(4p): |e| <= 2 kappa Lambda R^-1 (t/R)^(-n/p)(1 + t^-n I)
Integrating factor F with e^(-Lambda/2) <= F <= e^(Lambda/2), |F-1| <= Lambda (t/R)^(1-n/p), and Phi' = F t^-n J' >= 0
Tonelli and substitution bound integral t^-n J' by (1+eps)^n times the annular integral
Fixed-eps inequalities, then eps -> 0 using right-continuity of closed-ball masses: (G1), (G2)
Lower density omega_n at points of spt V via (G1) at nearby density points (theta >= 1 a.e.)
Phi(s) >= omega_n gives the third assertion e^-Lambda (omega_n - Lambda) <= s^-n mu(B_s(y))

subproblems.title: Pinched mass bounds near the origin (Simon 5.2.4, fact P)
subproblems.statement: For n >= 1, l, p > n there is delta_P in (0, 1/8] such that: if 0 < delta <= delta_P and 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho) holds for a contract rectifiable varifold V in an open U with generalized mean curvature H, then for every y with |y| <= 3 delta rho and every 0 < s <= rho/2: mu(B_s(y)) <= 2 omega_n s^n, and if moreover y in spt V then mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n/2 (mu = V.weight, closed balls).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ δP : ℝ, 0 < δP ∧ δP ≤ 1 / 8 ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ δP → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ y : Amb n ℓ, ‖y‖ ≤ 3 * (δ * ρ) → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ ρ / 2 → V.weight (closedBall y s) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * unitBallVolume n * s ^ n) ∧ (y ∈ V.support → ENNReal.ofReal (unitBallVolume n * s ^ n / 2) ≤ V.weight (closedBall y s))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 5, 2.4 (derived there from 4.7 and 4.9 of Ch. 4), in the corrected form (P.i)-(P.ii) of the parent proof, with Lambda = 4p delta/(p-n).

Notation. mu := V.weight, omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0, kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0, Lambda_t := 4pt/(p-n) = t/kappa for t >= 0, B_s(y) closed balls.

1. Choice of delta_P. The functions g_+(t) := e^(2 Lambda_t)(1+t)(1-3t)^-n + 2 e^(Lambda_t) Lambda_t/omega_n and g_-(t) := e^(-Lambda_t)(1 - Lambda_t/omega_n) are continuous on [0, 1/8] with g_+(0) = g_-(0) = 1. Choose delta_P with 0 < delta_P <= min{1/8, kappa} such that g_+(t) <= 2 and g_-(t) >= 1/2 for all t in [0, delta_P].
2. Let 0 < delta <= delta_P, 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2. Put Lambda := Lambda_delta = 4p delta/(p-n); then Lambda <= 1 (delta <= kappa). Put R_y := (1 - 3 delta) rho >= 5 rho/8 > rho/2 >= s. Then B_(R_y)(y) is contained in B_rho(0), since |x| <= |y| + R_y <= rho for x in B_(R_y)(y). Hence the monotonicity child (lip_approx_monotonicity) applies with this Lambda, centre y and radius R = R_y.
3. Upper bound. For every r in [s, R_y), the first assertion of the monotonicity child gives mu(B_s(y))/s^n <= e^(2 Lambda) mu(B_r(y))/r^n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda, and mu(B_r(y)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n by 2.3 (B_r(y) is contained in B_rho(0)). The right side e^(2 Lambda)(1 + delta) omega_n rho^n r^-n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda is continuous in r; letting r increase to R_y gives mu(B_s(y))/s^n <= e^(2 Lambda)(1 + delta) omega_n (1 - 3 delta)^-n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda = omega_n g_+(delta) <= 2 omega_n. Since mu(B_s(y)) < infinity (compact subset of U), this is the inequality V.weight(closedBall y s) <= ofReal(2 omega_n s^n).
4. Lower bound. Let y in spt V. The third assertion of the monotonicity child (with r := s, so s <= r < R_y) gives mu(B_s(y))/s^n >= e^(-Lambda)(omega_n - Lambda) = omega_n g_-(delta) >= omega_n/2, i.e. ofReal(omega_n s^n/2) <= V.weight(closedBall y s).

With Lambda = 4p delta/(p-n) <= 1 and R_y = (1-3 delta) rho, the ball B_(R_y)(y) lies in B_rho(0) and s < R_y
Upper bound: first monotonicity assertion with mu(B_r(y)) <= (1+delta) omega_n rho^n, then r -> R_y gives omega_n g_+(delta) <= 2 omega_n
Lower bound for y in spt V: third monotonicity assertion gives omega_n g_-(delta) >= omega_n/2

subproblems.title: Vitali 5r-covering estimate for two measures (fact Cov)
subproblems.statement: Let N in N, nu and Psi measures on R^N, S and W subsets of R^N, r : R^N -> R, R_0 in R and M in [0, infinity]. If for every y in S: 0 < r(y) <= R_0, B_(r(y))(y) is contained in W, and nu(S cap B_(5 r(y))(y)) <= M Psi(B_(r(y))(y)), then nu(S) <= M Psi(W).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (ν Ψ : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))) (S W : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))) (r : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) → ℝ) (R₀ : ℝ) (M : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ y ∈ S, 0 < r y ∧ r y ≤ R₀ ∧ closedBall y (r y) ⊆ W ∧ ν (S ∩ closedBall y (5 * r y)) ≤ M * Ψ (closedBall y (r y))) → ν S ≤ M * Ψ W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, 3.4 (5-times covering lemma) followed by the summation used in the proof of Lemma 2.6 (Ch. 5) and in steps 3 and 9 of the parent proof; fact (Cov) of the parent proof.

1. If S is empty, nu(S) = 0 and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise consider the family of closed balls B_y := B_(r(y))(y), y in S; by hypothesis 0 < r(y) <= R_0, so the radii are bounded.
2. 5-times covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall with tau = 5 > 3): there is a subset S' of S such that the balls B_b, b in S', are pairwise disjoint and for every a in S there is b in S' with B_a contained in B_(5 r(b))(b). Since r(a) > 0, a lies in B_a, hence a lies in S cap B_(5 r(b))(b).
3. S' is countable: the open balls B^o_(r(b))(b), b in S', are nonempty (r(b) > 0), open and pairwise disjoint (being contained in the disjoint closed balls), and R^N is separable (Mathlib Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_isOpen).
4. By step 2, S is contained in the countable union over b in S' of S cap B_(5 r(b))(b). By countable subadditivity of nu and the hypothesis, nu(S) <= sum_(b in S') nu(S cap B_(5 r(b))(b)) <= sum_(b in S') M Psi(B_b) = M sum_(b in S') Psi(B_b) (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left; valid also for M = infinity).
5. The closed balls B_b, b in S', are measurable, pairwise disjoint and contained in W, and S' is countable, so sum_(b in S') Psi(B_b) = Psi(union_(b in S') B_b) <= Psi(W). Hence nu(S) <= M Psi(W).
proof_key_steps: Bounded radii 0 < r(y) <= R_0
Vitali 5r selection: disjoint subfamily S' with every B_a inside some B_(5 r(b))(b)
S' is countable (disjoint nonempty open interiors in a separable space)
Countable subadditivity of nu and the hypothesis bound nu(S) by M times the sum of Psi(B_b)
Countable additivity of Psi on the disjoint balls inside W gives nu(S) <= M Psi(W)

subproblems.title: Lipschitz extension into R^l with exact sup bound (fact Ext plus radial retraction)
subproblems.statement: Let A be a subset of R^n, g : R^n -> R^l, M >= 0 and R_0 >= 0 with |g(x) - g(z)| <= M |x - z| for x, z in A and |g(x)| <= R_0 for x in A. Then there is f : R^n -> R^l with f = g on A, |f(x) - f(z)| <= sqrt(l) M |x - z| for all x, z, and |f(x)| <= R_0 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (A : Set (Rn n)) (g : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (M R₀ : ℝ), 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ R₀ → (∀ x ∈ A, ∀ z ∈ A, ‖g x - g z‖ ≤ M * ‖x - z‖) → (∀ x ∈ A, ‖g x‖ ≤ R₀) → ∃ f : Rn n → Rn ℓ, (∀ x ∈ A, f x = g x) ∧ (∀ x z, ‖f x - f z‖ ≤ Real.sqrt ℓ * M * ‖x - z‖) ∧ ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ R₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, 1.2 (McShane extension), applied componentwise as in fact (Ext) of the parent proof, followed by the radial retraction of step 5 of the parent proof (correction (iv): exact sup bound).

1. If A is empty, f := 0 has all three properties (|0 - 0| = 0 and |0| = 0 <= R_0). Assume A is nonempty.
2. For j < l let g_j(x) := (g(x))_j. For x, z in A, |g_j(x) - g_j(z)| <= |g(x) - g(z)| <= M |x - z|. By McShane's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2: h_j(x) := inf_(z in A) (g_j(z) + M |x - z|); Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real with constant M.toNNReal) there is h_j : R^n -> R with h_j = g_j on A and |h_j(x) - h_j(z)| <= M |x - z| for all x, z.
3. Let h(x) in R^l have coordinates h_j(x). Then h = g on A and |h(x) - h(z)|^2 = sum_(j<l) |h_j(x) - h_j(z)|^2 <= l M^2 |x - z|^2, i.e. |h(x) - h(z)| <= sqrt(l) M |x - z|.
4. Radial retraction. Define pi : R^l -> R^l by pi(v) := v if |v| <= R_0 and pi(v) := (R_0/|v|) v if |v| > R_0. Then |pi(v)| <= R_0, pi(v) = v whenever |v| <= R_0, and pi is the nearest-point projection onto the closed convex set B := {w : |w| <= R_0}: it satisfies the variational inequality <v - pi(v), w - pi(v)> <= 0 for all w in B (trivial if |v| <= R_0; if |v| > R_0, v - pi(v) = (1 - R_0/|v|) v and <v, w - R_0 v/|v|> = <v, w> - R_0 |v| <= |v| R_0 - R_0 |v| = 0). Adding the variational inequalities for v (tested with w = pi(v')) and for v' (tested with w = pi(v)) gives |pi(v) - pi(v')|^2 <= <v - v', pi(v) - pi(v')> <= |v - v'| |pi(v) - pi(v')|, hence pi is 1-Lipschitz. (If R_0 = 0 then pi = 0.)
5. Put f := pi o h. For x in A, |h(x)| = |g(x)| <= R_0, so f(x) = h(x) = g(x). For all x, z, |f(x) - f(z)| <= |h(x) - h(z)| <= sqrt(l) M |x - z|, and |f(x)| <= R_0.
proof_key_steps: Empty A: take f = 0
Each coordinate g_j is M-Lipschitz on A; extend by McShane to an M-Lipschitz h_j on R^n
h = (h_j) agrees with g on A and is sqrt(l) M-Lipschitz
The radial retraction onto the closed R_0-ball is 1-Lipschitz and fixes the ball
f = retraction o h keeps the values of g on A, the Lipschitz bound and |f| <= R_0

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of a rotated 1-Lipschitz graph over a ball (fact Gr)
subproblems.statement: For n >= 1, l, a linear isometry q of R^(n+l), f : R^n -> R^l with |f(x) - f(z)| <= |x - z| for all x, z, c in R^n and r >= 0: H^n(q(graph of f over the closed ball B^n_r(c))) <= 2^(n/2) omega_n r^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ), (∀ x z, ‖f x - f z‖ ≤ ‖x - z‖) → ∀ (c : Rn n) (r : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (q '' graphOver f (closedBall c r)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * unitBallVolume n * r ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (Gr) of the parent proof (Lipschitz images and H^n = L^n on R^n; Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i) and Ch. 1, 2.10).

1. Let Gamma : R^n -> R^(n+l), Gamma(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)). Since graphOver f D is the image of D under x -> graphPoint x (f x), q '' graphOver f (closedBall c r) = Gamma(closedBall c r).
2. Gamma is sqrt(2)-Lipschitz: by the graph-coordinates child (lip_approx_graph_coordinates), (i) and (ii), and since q is a linear isometry, |Gamma(x) - Gamma(z)|^2 = |graphPoint (x - z) (f x - f z)|^2 = |x - z|^2 + |f x - f z|^2 <= 2 |x - z|^2.
3. A K-Lipschitz map multiplies the n-dimensional Hausdorff measure by at most K^n (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le; for the normalised muHE[n], which is a constant multiple of muH[n], SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). Hence H^n(Gamma(closedBall c r)) <= (sqrt 2)^n H^n(closedBall c r), where on the right H^n = muHE[n] on R^n.
4. On R^n, muHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and for r >= 0, Lebesgue measure of closedBall c r is r^n pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2 + 1) = omega_n r^n (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_closedBall, with sqrt(pi)^n = pi^(n/2) and omega_n = unitBallVolume n).
5. Therefore H^n(q '' graphOver f (closedBall c r)) <= (sqrt 2)^n omega_n r^n = 2^(n/2) omega_n r^n.
proof_key_steps: Write the set as the image of closedBall c r under Gamma(x) = q(graphPoint x (f x))
Gamma is sqrt(2)-Lipschitz by the graph-coordinates identities and 1-Lipschitz f
Lipschitz image bound for muHE[n]: factor (sqrt 2)^n
muHE[n] = volume on R^n and volume of the closed r-ball is omega_n r^n

subproblems.title: Measure of the complement of the good set (Simon 5.2.6, estimate (6))
subproblems.statement: For n >= 1, l, p > n there are delta_0 > 0 and C_0 >= 0 such that: if 0 < delta <= delta_0, 2.3 holds, sigma_0 = delta rho, T is any linear subspace and b > 0, then mu(B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) minus G') <= (C_0/b) integral_(B_(sigma_0)(0)) hsNormSq(p_x - p_T) dmu, where G' is the set of y in spt V with integral_(B_(s/2)(y)) hsNormSq(p_x - p_T) dmu <= b s^n for all s in (0, sigma_0/2].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ δ₀ C₀ : ℝ, 0 < δ₀ ∧ 0 ≤ C₀ ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ δ₀ → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ (T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)) (b : ℝ), 0 < b → V.weight (closedBall 0 (3 * (δ * ρ) / 4) \ {y | y ∈ V.support ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ δ * ρ / 2 → ∫ x in closedBall y (s / 2), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection) ∂V.weight ≤ b * s ^ n}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C₀ / b * ∫ x in closedBall 0 (δ * ρ), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection) ∂V.weight)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.6, estimate (6) (step 3 of the parent proof), for an arbitrary subspace T and threshold b.

Constants. Let delta_P be given by the pinched-density child (lip_approx_pinched_density) for n, l, p, and set delta_0 := delta_P (> 0, <= 1/8) and C_0 := 2 omega_n (5/2)^n (>= 0), omega_n := unitBallVolume n.

Let 0 < delta <= delta_0, 2.3 hold, sigma_0 := delta rho, T a subspace with projection P := p_T, b > 0. Write mu := V.weight, tau(x) := hsNormSq(p_x - P) >= 0 and tilt(A) := integral_A tau dmu.
1. Integrability. Every closed ball contained in B_rho(0) is a compact subset of U, so by the tangent-structure child (lip_approx_tangent_structure (b)) tau is mu-integrable on it and tilt of it is finite. Let Psi be the measure A -> integral_A ofReal(tau) dmu (mu.withDensity); for such balls B, Psi(B) = ofReal(tilt(B)).
2. Let G' := {y in spt V : tilt(B_(s/2)(y)) <= b s^n for all s in (0, sigma_0/2]} and S := (B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) cap spt V) minus G'. Then B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) minus G' is contained in S union (B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) minus spt V). As B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) is contained in B_rho(0), a subset of U, and spt V = U cap spt mu, the second set is contained in the complement of spt mu, which is mu-null (the complement of the support is a countable union of open mu-null sets in the second countable space R^(n+l)). Hence mu(B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) minus G') <= mu(S).
3. For y in S choose s_y in (0, sigma_0/2] with tilt(B_(s_y/2)(y)) > b s_y^n (this is the negation of the condition defining G', as y lies in spt V) and put r_y := s_y/2 in (0, sigma_0/4].
4. For y in S: (i) B_(r_y)(y) is contained in B_(sigma_0)(0), since |y| + r_y <= 3 sigma_0/4 + sigma_0/4; (ii) |y| <= 3 sigma_0/4 <= 3 delta rho and 0 < 5 r_y = 5 s_y/2 <= 5 sigma_0/4 <= rho/2 (delta <= 1/8), so the pinched-density child gives mu(S cap B_(5 r_y)(y)) <= mu(B_(5 s_y/2)(y)) <= 2 omega_n (5 s_y/2)^n = C_0 s_y^n < (C_0/b) tilt(B_(r_y)(y)) = (C_0/b) Psi(B_(r_y)(y)).
5. Apply the Vitali child (lip_approx_vitali_bound) with N = n + l, nu := mu, the measure Psi, the set S, W := B_(sigma_0)(0), radii r_y, R_0 := sigma_0/4 and M := ofReal(C_0/b): mu(S) <= ofReal(C_0/b) Psi(B_(sigma_0)(0)) = ofReal(C_0/b) ofReal(tilt(B_(sigma_0)(0))).
6. By steps 2 and 5, mu(B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) minus G') <= ofReal((C_0/b) tilt(B_(sigma_0)(0))) (tilt >= 0, C_0/b >= 0).
proof_key_steps: Tilt integrands are integrable on closed balls in B_rho(0) (tangent-structure child); Psi = tilt measure
Outside spt V the ball is mu-null, so it suffices to bound mu(S), S = bad points of spt V
Each bad y has a radius s_y with tilt(B_(s_y/2)(y)) > b s_y^n
Pinched density bounds mu(B_(5 s_y/2)(y)) <= 2 omega_n (5/2)^n s_y^n < (C_0/b) Psi(B_(s_y/2)(y))
Vitali child with W = B_(sigma_0)(0) gives mu(S) <= (C_0/b) tilt(B_(sigma_0)(0))

subproblems.title: Height bound and Lipschitz-graph property of the good set (Simon 5.2.6, (3)-(4))
subproblems.statement: Assume AffineApproximationLemma. For n >= 1, l, p > n there are C_0 > 0 and delta_0 > 0 such that for all beta > 0, L in (0,1], 0 < delta <= delta_0 with delta <= (beta L)^(2n+2), 2.3, and every linear isometry q with T_0 = rotatedPlane q, P = p_(T_0), sigma_0 = delta rho: if integral_(B_(sigma_0)(0)) hsNormSq(p_x - P) dmu <= beta^2 L^2 sigma_0^n, then (1) dist(x, T_0) <= C_0 beta L sigma_0 for every x in spt V cap B_(2 sigma_0)(0), and (2) for y_1, y_2 in spt V cap B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) such that integral_(B_(s/2)(y_1)) hsNormSq(p_x - P) dmu <= beta^2 L^2 s^n for all s in (0, sigma_0/2], |(y_2 - y_1) - P(y_2 - y_1)| <= C_0 beta L |y_2 - y_1|.
subproblems.lean_statement: AffineApproximationLemma → ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ C₀ δ₀ : ℝ, 0 < C₀ ∧ 0 < δ₀ ∧ ∀ β L : ℝ, 0 < β → 0 < L → L ≤ 1 → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ δ₀ → δ ≤ (β * L) ^ (2 * n + 2) → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ, ∫ x in closedBall 0 (δ * ρ), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection) ∂V.weight ≤ β ^ 2 * L ^ 2 * (δ * ρ) ^ n → (∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall 0 (2 * (δ * ρ)), infDist x (rotatedPlane q : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ C₀ * β * L * (δ * ρ)) ∧ ∀ y₁ ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall 0 (3 * (δ * ρ) / 4), ∀ y₂ ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall 0 (3 * (δ * ρ) / 4), (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ δ * ρ / 2 → ∫ x in closedBall y₁ (s / 2), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection) ∂V.weight ≤ β ^ 2 * L ^ 2 * s ^ n) → ‖(y₂ - y₁) - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection (y₂ - y₁)‖ ≤ C₀ * β * L * ‖y₂ - y₁‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.6, inequalities (3)-(4) (steps 2 and 4 of the parent proof), in the contract normalisation with an arbitrary rotation q; correction (iii): pairs at distance > sigma_0/2 are handled by the height bound.

Assume AffineApproximationLemma. Fix n >= 1, l, p > n. Let C_sib > 0 be its constant for (n, l, p) and C_A := max{C_sib, 1}; both inequalities of the lemma remain true with C_A in place of C_sib (C_A^-1 <= C_sib^-1 in the first, C_A >= C_sib in the second). Let delta_P be given by the pinched-density child (lip_approx_pinched_density); tilt integrability comes from the tangent-structure child (lip_approx_tangent_structure). Put omega_n := unitBallVolume n, alpha := 1/(2n+2), C_1 := 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2, C_2 := (4(1 + C_1)/omega_n)^(1/2), C_3 := 2 C_A + 2 C_2, C_5 := (2^(n+2)(1 + C_1)/omega_n)^(1/2), C_6 := C_A + C_5, and C_0 := max{C_6, 4 C_3} > 0, delta_0 := min{1/4, delta_P} > 0. These depend only on n, l, p.

Let beta > 0, L in (0,1], 0 < delta <= delta_0 with delta <= (beta L)^(2n+2), 2.3, q a linear isometry, T_0 := rotatedPlane q, P := p_(T_0), sigma_0 := delta rho, mu := V.weight, and assume tilt(B_(sigma_0)(0)) := integral_(B_(sigma_0)(0)) |p_x - P|^2 dmu <= beta^2 L^2 sigma_0^n. Here |.| on linear maps is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm, with hsNormSq its square).
1. Preliminaries. (a) delta^alpha <= beta L (monotonicity of t -> t^alpha) and delta <= delta^alpha <= 1 (delta <= 1). (b) If t > 0 and B_t(z) is contained in B_rho(0), then K(z,t) := V.scaledLpNorm H p z t <= delta: K(z,t)^p = t^(p-n) integral_(B_t(z)) |H|^p <= rho^(p-n) integral_(B_rho(0)) |H|^p <= delta^p (t <= rho, p > n). (c) For subspaces T, T' and any x: |p_T - p_(T')|^2 <= 2 |p_x - p_T|^2 + 2 |p_x - p_(T')|^2 (triangle inequality for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm and (a+b)^2 <= 2a^2 + 2b^2). (d) |A v| <= |A| |v| (operator norm <= Hilbert-Schmidt norm, Cauchy-Schwarz). (e) For a subspace T and v: |v - p_T v| = dist(v, T) (Mathlib Submodule.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist). (f) Tilt integrands are integrable on closed balls contained in B_rho(0) (tangent-structure child (b)), and such balls have finite mu-measure.
 (g) Affine approximation output: let xi in spt V cap B_(delta rho)(0) and 0 < sigma <= 2 delta rho. The lemma (applicable since 0 < delta <= 1/4 and 2.3 holds) gives an n-plane T' with (i) sigma^-1 heightSup(xi, sigma, T') <= C_A delta^alpha, hence dist(x - xi, T') <= C_A delta^alpha sigma for every x in spt V cap B_sigma(xi); and (ii) C_A^-1 (sigma^-n integral_(B_(sigma/2)(xi)) |p_x - p_(T')|^2 dmu)^(1/2) <= sigma^-1 heightSup(xi, sigma, T') + K(xi, sigma) <= C_A delta^alpha + delta <= (C_A + 1) delta^alpha, using (b) (B_sigma(xi) is contained in B_(3 delta rho)(0), a subset of B_rho(0)) and (a); hence integral_(B_(sigma/2)(xi)) |p_x - p_(T')|^2 dmu <= C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 delta^(2 alpha) sigma^n.
2. Height bound (first conclusion). Apply (g) with xi = 0 (0 in spt V by 2.3) and sigma = 2 sigma_0: there is T* with dist(x, T*) <= 2 C_A delta^alpha sigma_0 for x in spt V cap B_(2 sigma_0)(0) and integral_(B_(sigma_0)(0)) |p_x - p_(T*)|^2 <= C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 delta^(2 alpha) (2 sigma_0)^n = C_1 delta^(2 alpha) sigma_0^n <= C_1 beta^2 L^2 sigma_0^n. Integrate (c) (T = T_0, T' = T*) over B_(sigma_0)(0) and use mu(B_(sigma_0)(0)) >= omega_n sigma_0^n/2 (pinched-density child, lower bound at y = 0 in spt V, s = sigma_0 <= rho/2): (omega_n sigma_0^n/2) |P - p_(T*)|^2 <= 2 tilt(B_(sigma_0)(0)) + 2 C_1 beta^2 L^2 sigma_0^n <= 2(1 + C_1) beta^2 L^2 sigma_0^n, so |P - p_(T*)| <= C_2 beta L. For x in spt V cap B_(2 sigma_0)(0), by (e) and (d): dist(x, T_0) = |x - P x| <= |x - p_(T*) x| + |(p_(T*) - P) x| <= 2 C_A delta^alpha sigma_0 + 2 C_2 beta L sigma_0 <= C_3 beta L sigma_0 <= C_0 beta L sigma_0.
3. Graph estimate (second conclusion). Let y_1, y_2 in spt V cap B_(3 sigma_0/4)(0) with integral_(B_(s/2)(y_1)) |p_x - P|^2 dmu <= beta^2 L^2 s^n for all s in (0, sigma_0/2]. If y_1 = y_2 both sides vanish. Otherwise let s := |y_2 - y_1| in (0, 3 sigma_0/2] and v := y_2 - y_1.
 (a) Case s <= sigma_0/2. Apply (g) with xi = y_1 (|y_1| <= 3 sigma_0/4 <= delta rho) and sigma = s (<= 2 delta rho): there is T_1 with dist(y_2 - y_1, T_1) <= C_A delta^alpha s (y_2 lies in spt V cap B_s(y_1)) and integral_(B_(s/2)(y_1)) |p_x - p_(T_1)|^2 <= C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 delta^(2 alpha) s^n <= C_1 beta^2 L^2 s^n. Source: Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.6, inequalities (9)-(10) (step 7 of the parent proof), with corrections (i) Lambda = 4p delta/(p-n) and (v) the annulus is B_(3s) minus B_s and the ball B_(3s)(zeta) is controlled by the pinched bounds at a nearby support point.

Constants. kappa := (p-n)/(4p), omega_n := unitBallVolume n, delta_P from the pinched-density child (lip_approx_pinched_density), A_8 := 72 * 3^n e^2/omega_n, and
 eps := (4 A_8 omega_n 5^n)^(-1/2) > 0, C_0 := 2 A_8 > 0, delta_0 := min{delta_P, kappa, 3^-n omega_n (p-n)/(32 e p)} > 0.
Let 0 < delta <= delta_0, 2.3 hold, sigma_0 := delta rho, T a subspace, P := p_T, Q := I - P, F closed with |Q(x - z)| <= eps |x - z| for x, z in F, zeta in F with |zeta| <= 17 sigma_0/32 and 0 < d := infDist(zeta, spt V) <= sigma_0/16; put s := d/2, mu := V.weight, tau(x) := hsNormSq(p_x - P), tilt(A) := integral_A tau dmu, Lambda := 4p delta/(p-n) (<= 1 since delta <= kappa).
1. Nearest support point. spt mu is closed and contains spt V, which contains 0, so there is y in spt mu with |y - zeta| = infDist(zeta, spt mu) <= infDist(zeta, spt V) = d. Then |y| <= 17 sigma_0/32 + sigma_0/16 = 19 sigma_0/32 < rho, so y lies in B_rho(0), contained in U, hence y in spt V = U cap spt mu, so |y - zeta| >= d. Thus |y - zeta| = d = 2s and infDist(zeta, spt mu) = d. The open ball B^o_d(zeta) does not meet spt mu, so mu(B^o_d(zeta)) = 0 (the complement of spt mu is mu-null), and since s < d, mu(B_s(zeta)) = 0.
2. Monotonicity at zeta. Put R := (1 - 3 delta) rho >= 5 rho/8. Since |zeta| <= 17 sigma_0/32 <= 3 delta rho, B_R(zeta) is contained in B_rho(0); and 0 < s <= 3s <= 3 sigma_0/32 < R. The second assertion of the monotonicity child (lip_approx_monotonicity; centre zeta, r := 3s) together with mu(B_s(zeta)) = 0 gives
 (3s)^-n mu(B_(3s)(zeta)) <= 2 e^Lambda Lambda + e^(2 Lambda) integral_(B_(3s)(zeta) minus B_s(zeta)) |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 |x - zeta|^(-n-2) dmu <= 2 e Lambda + e^2 s^(-n-2) I,
 where I := integral_(B_(3s)(zeta)) |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 dmu: on the annulus |x - zeta| > s, and the integrand of I is nonnegative, bounded by 9 s^2, and mu-measurable (tangent-structure child lip_approx_tangent_structure), while mu(B_(3s)(zeta)) < infinity.
3. Lower bound. B_s(y) is contained in B_(3s)(zeta) (|y - zeta| = 2s). By the pinched-density child (y in spt V, |y| <= 19 sigma_0/32 <= 3 delta rho, s <= rho/2), mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n/2, so 3^-n omega_n/2 <= (3s)^-n mu(B_(3s)(zeta)) <= 2 e Lambda + e^2 s^(-n-2) I. Because delta <= 3^-n omega_n (p-n)/(32 e p), 2 e Lambda = 8 e p delta/(p-n) <= 3^-n omega_n/4, hence s^(n+2) <= 4 * 3^n e^2 omega_n^-1 I.
4. Upper bound for I. For every x, p_x^perp = Q + (P - p_x), so |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 <= 2 |Q(x - zeta)|^2 + 2 |P - p_x|^2 |x - zeta|^2 <= 2 |Q(x - zeta)|^2 + 18 s^2 tau(x) on B_(3s)(zeta) (operator norm <= Hilbert-Schmidt norm). For x in F cap B_(3s)(zeta), |Q(x - zeta)| <= eps |x - zeta| <= 3 eps s (zeta in F); for every x in B_(3s)(zeta), |Q(x - zeta)| <= |x - zeta| <= 3s. Moreover B_(3s)(zeta) is contained in B_(5s)(y), so mu(B_(3s)(zeta)) <= mu(B_(5s)(y)) <= 2 omega_n 5^n s^n by the pinched-density child (|y| <= 3 delta rho, 5s <= rho/2). F is closed, so B_(3s)(zeta) splits into the measurable parts B_(3s)(zeta) cap F and B_(3s)(zeta) minus F, and tau is integrable on B_(3s)(zeta) (tangent-structure child). Therefore
 I <= 18 eps^2 s^2 mu(B_(3s)(zeta)) + 18 s^2 mu(B_(3s)(zeta) minus F) + 18 s^2 tilt(B_(3s)(zeta)) <= 18 s^2 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_(3s)(zeta) minus F) + tilt(B_(3s)(zeta))].
5. Conclusion. By steps 3 and 4, s^n <= A_8 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_(3s)(zeta) minus F) + tilt(B_(3s)(zeta))]. Since A_8 * 2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 = 1/2, s^n <= 2 A_8 [mu(B_(3s)(zeta) minus F) + tilt(B_(3s)(zeta))] = C_0 [...], which, written in [0, infinity] with tilt >= 0, is ofReal(s^n) <= ofReal(C_0) (V.weight(B_(3s)(zeta) minus F) + ofReal(tilt(B_(3s)(zeta)))).
proof_key_steps: Nearest point y of spt mu to zeta lies in spt V at distance exactly d = 2s, so mu(B_s(zeta)) = 0
Second monotonicity assertion at zeta with radii s and 3s: (3s)^-n mu(B_(3s)(zeta)) <= 2e Lambda + e^2 s^(-n-2) I
B_s(y) inside B_(3s)(zeta) and the pinched lower bound at y, with 2e Lambda <= 3^-n omega_n/4, give s^(n+2) <= 4 3^n e^2 omega_n^-1 I
p_x^perp = Q + (P - p_x), the cone property on F and the pinched upper bound bound I by 18 s^2 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_(3s) minus F) + tilt]
eps^2 = 1/(4 A_8 omega_n 5^n) absorbs the first term: s^n <= 2 A_8 [mu(B_(3s)(zeta) minus F) + tilt(B_(3s)(zeta))]
